regime: Choppy Fade (Shutdown Pop Then Fade, NQ Flipped Bearish)
summary: The government shut down and the tape could not make up its mind. The Nasdaq popped overnight to 31,150 well past 31,000, reversed hard to a 30,531 low, flipped its ATR stop bearish, and clawed back to close 30,770.5, up a token 0.14 percent but below that flipped stop. The S&P was flat at 7,725 and still below a falling stop, so tech and the broad market are both heavy under their trend lines. Gold bounced 0.67 percent to 4,177.6 but stalled under its 4,182 flipped stop, while crude was the one clean trend, up 2.88 percent to 92.93 above a rising stop. Jobless claims fell to 197K and ISM held 54.5, while the 10-year yield spiked to a 24-year-high 5.33 percent intraday before easing.

event.crossAsset: Crude ripped +2.88% above a rising stop, gold bounced +0.67% but stalled under its flipped stop, ES was flat +0.05% below a falling stop; the 10-year spiked to 5.33% then eased and the VIX sat at 16.39.

risk.note: Throttle stays REDUCED. The shutdown cleared without a volatility spike but the tape gave a split, low-conviction read: NQ flipped its stop bearish on a green close, ES stayed heavy below a falling stop and gold stalled under its flip, with only crude trending cleanly. With the September jobs report likely delayed, Friday loses its usual catalyst, so keep size measured and let the stops confirm a trend before adding. Most prop firms restrict trading around scheduled releases, so check your firm's news rule before any delayed-data headlines.

psychology: A shutdown headline, an overnight rip past 31,000, then a full session give-back. Anyone who chased the overnight high spent the day in pain. The Nasdaq closed green but below a stop that flipped bearish, and a green number on the screen can hide a change of trend underneath it. The ATR stop flipped down even while the close stayed positive, and that flip is the more honest read of who had control today. Predicting the shutdown was never the job. Sizing for a tape that keeps reversing, and letting the stop guide your bias, is where the edge lives.

fullReport.title: NY Opening Range / HTA OPEN (MNQ)
fullReport.html: Opening range high 30,856.25, low 30,734.25, width 122 points (about 0.40 percent). Break DOWN at 13:45 UTC, first 5-minute close under the range at 30,709.25. NYVWAP 30,711.05, and price closed 30,773.5 back inside the range and above NYVWAP. HOF VWAP 30,707.87. No clean playbook entry confirmed, but this was textbook Back-in-Range habitat: a down-break that then closes back inside the range. Filter state (Friday): no CPI, no FOMC, not a Monday or Wednesday, so all four plays are eligible. Lesson: a break that closes back inside the range is a fade, so wait for acceptance outside the range before trusting it.

fullReport.title: Momentum Breakout (Regime Filter)
fullReport.html: No signal fired. ROC(12) is negative at -0.24 percent over the last twelve hours, so momentum points down despite the green close. Price closed 30,770, just above the 50-EMA near 30,760, so the regime filter is not blocking and E3v2 stays borderline rather than off. Relative volume is disclaimed on a continuous contract. The breakout long stays parked until a real volume and momentum thrust clears the 50-EMA.

fullReport.title: AVWAP Deviation Band Reversal (MNQ)
fullReport.html: AVWAP center 30,713 (1 sigma about 81 points). Bands: plus 2 sigma 30,875, plus 3 sigma 30,956; minus 2 sigma 30,551, minus 3 sigma 30,470. Price closed 30,770, inside plus 1 sigma (30,794). No plus or minus 2 sigma exhaustion tag today, so there is no reversion-grade setup yet. Watch a tag of plus 2 sigma near 30,875 or minus 2 sigma near 30,551 for a fade back toward AVWAP.
